newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Thai Submicron sees listing Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Thai Submicron sees listing Q1 1997.

text.p: Submicron Technology Public, Thailand's first semiconductor foundry, hopes to be listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand by the first quarter of next year, top company executives said on Wednesday.
Its US$850 million plant, built to cash in on the growing electronic industry, is expected to be ready for a test run early next year and be operational by June as scheduled, they told Reuters.

"The company has borrowed money and now is looking at the equity side. We hope to float 50 million shares through initial public offering by the end of this year," Submicron's chief financial officer Kittiya Todhanakasem said.
"How much that will fetch I don't know. It depends on the market,' she said.
Submicron Technology was incorporated in 1991 under the name "Spectrum Electric Systems co. Ltd."

It changed its name to the present one in 1994 and signed a contract with Anderson Debart Pan of U.S. and Meissner & Wurst GmbH of Germany to design and manage the construction of the wafer fabrication plant, respectively.
In 1995, the company increased its registered capital to three billion baht and transformed into a public company. It then raised capital to five billion baht in 1996.
The company financed its plant through loans.

The factory will initially produce 500 integrated circuit wafers per week at the start-up and then increase that to 2,000 units per week by the end of 1997. It will reach full capacity of 5,000 units per week by 1998.
Glen Possley, the company president, said the rising world demand for electronic products will ensure the success of the project.

"The demand worldwide for electronic goods is still strong. You look at the semiconductor industry or electronic industry worldwide and in the past 25 years it grew by almost a 100 times," he told Reuters.
"In the next 25 years you can just bet that things are going to grow more...especially in this part of the world," he said.
Possley said the company had signed contracts with several clients who committed to buy all the company's output over the next five to seven years. A major client was Rockwell Semiconductor System.
"We expect that the company should be able to make profit on the third year of operation or by 1999," Kittiya added.
More than 80 percent of Submicron Technology is owned by Thailand's electronics tycoon Charn Uswachoke. The rest is owned by other financial institutions and companies.
